findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category/uncategorized_category_id were never overridden
findings.body: The migration does `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i` and later `execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'")[0]['value'].to_i`. In Discourse, a site_setting only has a row in the `site_settings` table if it was explicitly changed from its default. Both `embed_category` (default '') and `uncategorized_category_id` (default -1) are typically never explicitly set, so both queries will return zero rows. `result[0]` is then `nil`, and calling `['id']`/`['value']` on `nil` raises `NoMethodError`, which will fail the migration for the vast majority of installations, blocking deployment entirely.

findings.title: Unescaped string interpolation into INSERT statement (SQL injection / syntax errors)
findings.body: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"` interpolates `h` (a value read from the old `embeddable_hosts` site setting) directly into the SQL string without escaping/quoting. If that legacy value contains a single quote or other SQL metacharacters, the migration will fail with a syntax error or could execute unintended SQL. This should use parameterized SQL or `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote`.

findings.title: before_validation crashes with NoMethodError when host is nil
findings.body: The `before_validation` block calls `self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` and `self.host.sub!(/\/.*$/, '')` unconditionally. If `host` is nil (e.g. the admin submits the create/update form without a `host` value, which the controller does not guard against), this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil:NilClass` before validation even runs, resulting in an unhandled 500 error instead of a normal validation failure message.

findings.title: update/destroy actions crash with NoMethodError for a missing id
findings.body: In both `update` (`host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first`) and `destroy`, the controller does not check whether `host` is nil before calling `save_host(host)` or `host.destroy`. If `params[:id]` does not match any record (e.g., stale client state, race with another delete), this raises `NoMethodError` on `nil`, producing an unhandled 500 instead of a clean 404/error response.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents swapped with embeddable_host_fabricator.rb
findings.body: After this change, `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` contains only the `:embeddable_host` Fabricator definition, while the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, and `:private_category` Fabricators (the content that used to live in category_fabricator.rb). The file names no longer match their contents, which will mislead future maintainers looking for category or embeddable_host fabricators and increases the risk that one of these files gets incorrectly deleted/edited based on its name alone.

findings.title: New admin controllers lack behavioral test coverage
findings.body: Both `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb` only assert that the controller is a subclass of `Admin::AdminController`. Neither exercises the actual `create`, `update`, or `destroy` actions (success paths, validation failures, missing-record handling, serialization format), despite this PR introducing the entire embeddable-host CRUD surface. Real regressions in these new endpoints (e.g., the nil-record crashes in update/destroy, or the nil-host crash in the model) would not be caught by this test suite.

findings.title: saveChanges action is defined but never invoked
findings.body: The `saveChanges` action calls `this.get('embedding').update({})`, which performs a PUT to `/admin/customize/embedding`. However, `app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/embedding.hbs` only renders an "addHost" button and the per-host edit/delete controls; nothing in the template triggers the `saveChanges` action. This is dead code, and the corresponding `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` action is a no-op (it just re-serializes the current DB state), so this part of the exposed API has no real purpose as wired up.

findings.title: Host validation regex rejects valid modern TLDs
findings.body: `validates_format_of :host, :with => /\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i` restricts the TLD portion to 2-5 characters. Many legitimate modern gTLDs (e.g. `.london`, `.company`, `.photography`) exceed 5 characters and would be rejected by this validation, preventing admins from registering otherwise valid embeddable hosts using those domains.
